title: Route percentile insightboard with stream vs sync breakdown and tracing hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a consolidated insightboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model and API route with an explicit breakdown for streaming vs non-streaming requests. Add trace hooks (trace_id links) from each percentile cell, and validate metrics/log pipelines to ensure the new breakdowns are accurate and not sampling-biased.
background: We currently have multiple dashboards and ad-hoc panels showing latency percentiles by route or model, but there is no single view that (a) shows streaming vs sync latency side-by-side, (b) links directly to traces for outliers, and (c) couples metric health checks so on-call can trust the numbers. This ticket ties together tracing instrumentation, metric pipeline validation, and a UX that helps incident responders and SREs quickly find the root cause of percentile regressions.
scope:
- New insightboard in Console observability namespace that lists model x route rows and percentile columns (p50/p95/p99)
- Streaming vs non-streaming split per cell with small sparkline history
- Clickable trace links for samples above p95 that open APM traces filtered by trace_id
- Metric pipeline validation checks (aggregation correctness, tag presence, cardinality alerting)
- Lightweight sampling guidance to avoid high-cardinality blowup
- Smoke tests and rollout to staging then prod
design_notes: Dashboard will be implemented as a Grafana panel set in the observability repo. Each row keys off route_id and model_name tags. We will add an explicit tag io_mode={streaming, sync} emitted by the serving runtime. Percentiles are computed via the existing clickhouse metrics (latency_ms histogram) using quantileExact/approx queries with consistent aggregations across time windows. Trace links use a deterministic mapping trace_id -> external APM URL (opentelemetry collector + trace id stored in request logs). To limit cardinality, we will only tag model_name and route_id at the top level and avoid per-customer tags in this view.
implementation_notes:
- Runtime change: add io_mode tag to latency metrics and ensure route_id and model_name tags are populated (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2143)
- Metrics pipeline: add a ClickHouse materialized view that computes per-route/model/hr histograms (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/876)
- Dashboard: new Grafana dashboard JSON under observability/dashboards/route_percentiles_stream_sync.json (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/889)
- Logs: ensure request logs include trace_id and route_id for trace linking (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/logging/pull/332)
- Sampling: default trace sampling for product routes at 1% with dynamic bump to 10% when p95 exceeds threshold (config change in runtime-autoscaling repo)
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for every active model x route row in staging and prod
- Each percentile cell clearly displays streaming vs sync numbers and a 1h sparkline
- Clicking the p95/p99 value opens the APM trace view filtered to a sample trace_id
- Metrics pipeline unit tests and end-to-end smoke tests validate that percentiles reported by the dashboard match raw trace-percentiles within 2% for synthetic load
- Cardinality of the materialized view stays under budget (alert suppressed after verification or remediation plan documented)
rollout_plan:
1) Implement runtime tag changes and logging in a feature branch; run canary on staging.
2) Deploy ClickHouse materialized view in read-only mode and validate with historical queries.
3) Publish Grafana dashboard to staging; run synthetic load harness to compare with raw traces.
4) Enable in canary prod namespace with trace sampling bump available for on-call.
5) Full rollout after 48h of stable metrics and ops sign-off.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: adding io_mode tag increases metrics cardinality. Mitigation: limit tag to route-level only, use materialized rollups, and add a guardrail that rejects additional high-cardinality tags.
- Risk: trace sampling skew causes percentile mismatch. Mitigation: validate percentiles against unsampled synthetic runs and expose sampling rate metadata on the board.
- Risk: dashboard queries are expensive. Mitigation: rely on precomputed rollups and cache p99 for 1m windows.
metrics_to_monitor:
- percentiles_consistency_error: relative difference between dashboard percentiles and trace-derived percentiles (target < 2%)
- materialized_view_row_count and monthly cardinality
- dashboard_query_latency (95th)
- trace_link_success_rate (click -> trace opens)
